newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Ranbaxy sees end-97 U.S. launch.
newsitem.headline: India's Ranbaxy sees end-97 U.S. launch.

text.p: Ranbaxy Laboratories Ltd, India's largest pharmaceutical company, will launch its products in the United States towards the end of 1997, a company statement said on Tuesday.
The statement quoted the firm's president, D.S. Brar as saying: "Ranbaxy Pharmaceuticals Inc will be ready to launch products under its own label in the last quarter of 1997.
"We will source a basket of products from our alliance partners and through our own Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approvals."
The company expected to achieve higher growth rate than the industry average, and its enhancement through acquisitions of carefully selected brands, Brar said.

Ranbaxy acquired Croslands Research and some brands from Bombay-based Gufic in 1996/97 (April-March). The statement said that the operations of both acquisitions were synergising quickly with those of the company.
It added that the company was planning to launch several products in 1997/98, through its Pharma and Stancare divisions and, Croslands, Solus and Rexcel brands.
Earlier on Tuesday, the company announced a 14.2 percent increase in net profit to 1,542 million rupees in 1996/97 against 1,350 million in 1995/96.

The statement quoted chairman and managing director, Parvinder Singh saying: "Ranbaxy enhanced its strengths in all its business, both at home and overseas. It is on course to become a research-based international pharmaceutical company."

On his move to divest 6.0 percent equity overseas, Singh said: "In view of the concerns expressed by some investors, it is my intention to review this matter with an objective of....addressing their concerns...and the need to deleverage."
